Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

usRds 0.1.0.9000

  • NEWS.md added to record user-facing changes from here on. Earlier changes are described in the pull requests on GitHub (https://github.com/VagishHemmige/usRds/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged).

  • Claim extractors label HCFASAF code E as “Durable Medical Equipment”; it used to become NA, and establish_dx_date() then dropped those claims. Code Q is now “Quarterly dialysis (PMMIS)”, as in Appendix C, and unknown codes give a warning (#27).

  • adjust_costs_for_inflation() now finds the CPI for each claim’s month in any locale; in a non-English session every _ADJUSTED amount used to be NA (#105).

  • New check_repo_for_usrds_data() lists files in a project folder that look like USRDS data (data file types, USRDS file names, USRDS_ID columns), by path only, checking the files git would commit (#49).

  • New claims_followup_end() finds the last day of claims-based follow-up: the earliest of death, the end of Medicare-primary coverage, the date the claims are complete to, a study end date and a maximum length (#23).

  • establish_dx_date() gains date_as (date the diagnosis at the confirming claim, as before, or at the first claim), window_days (largest gap between two non-inpatient claims) and inpatient_types. REBUS inpatient stays (HCFASAF code M) now count as inpatient claims (#4).

  • get_IN_REV_costs() returns CLM_THRU, REV_DT and the revenue center CODE, so its output can be prorated, and drops revenue center 0001 total lines by default (drop_total_lines), which counted each claim twice (#112, #66).

  • get_PS_CLM_costs(remove_missing_values = TRUE) now drops claims with a missing CLM_PMT_AMT; the argument had no effect before (#54).

  • New prepare_medicare_coverage() builds the Medicare-primary coverage spells from the payer history once. Passing its result to verify_medicare_primary() skips rebuilding them on every call, which made checks inside a matching loop slow (#5).

  • verify_medicare_primary() gains payers, the payers that count as Medicare primary, as codes or labels; the default is still MPAB and MPO (#5).

  • verify_medicare_primary() accepts payer codes (MPAB, MPO) as well as their labels, merges coverage spans nested inside earlier ones, stops when coverage dates are not Dates, and warns about patients missing from the payer history it loads (#5).

Developed by Vagish Hemmige.
